In the modern digital age, the ability to type quickly and accurately has become an indispensable skill. From software developers writing thousands of lines of code to journalists crafting breaking news stories, efficient typing directly impacts productivity. The journey to typing mastery begins with understanding the fundamentals: proper finger placement on the home row, correct posture, and the discipline to look at the screen rather than the keyboard. With consistent daily practice, even beginners can achieve professional-level speeds within months.

The history of typing stretches back to the invention of the typewriter in the 1860s. Christopher Latham Sholes, along with Carlos Glidden and Samuel Soule, developed the first practical typewriter. The QWERTY layout was specifically designed to prevent mechanical jamming by spacing out commonly used letter pairs. Despite the advent of electronic keyboards that don't jam, QWERTY remains the dominant layout worldwide. Alternative layouts like Dvorak and Colemak claim improved efficiency, but QWERTY's entrenched position makes switching impractical for most users. Today, touch typing is taught in schools and professional training programs, recognized as a fundamental digital literacy skill.
